question: Does the queue absorb the backlog, and does every published event still land?

checks.name: every ping was accepted by the broker
the processor consumed some of the stream first
the queue still held the rest when it died
deliveries were refused while it was down
each held-back message was refused its whole delivery budget
the broker gave up on the held-back messages, as intended
everything the queue still held was dead-lettered, not lost
the replayer recovered every dead letter
nothing was left on the dead-letter topic
zero loss: rows written equals events published
one live row per distinct vehicle

notes: The corpus is filtered to one ping per idempotency key before publishing, so rows == published is a reachable assertion; a raw multi-snapshot capture re-sends about a third of its own observations and those deduplicate by design (experiment 4 measures that deliberately).

The local bridge retries a refused delivery immediately with no backoff, so the delivery budget is consumed faster here than a real push subscription would consume it. That makes dead-lettering easier to provoke, which is the point, but the outage duration is not comparable to a production one.
